description: Baseline: full ComfyUI benchmark on dev branch. Fixed sanity check (find pattern didn't match bin scripts).

asi.hypothesis: Baseline measurement of full ComfyUI benchmark

description: Avoid zero-fill + copy for full-block new writes. Also removed redundant ultracdc_chunk_count call (was computing chunk count just for a debug log). Huge win on lg_write_dura: 54s→20s.

asi.hypothesis: Skip zero-fill+copy for full-block writes to new blocks. Large files (dd bs=1M) write exactly one full block per FUSE message, all new extents, so every block hits the fast path. Removed redundant chunk counting for debug log.

description: Skip SurrealKV range scan when inode.size==0. Regression: 92,543→94,618 (+2.2%). Range scan overhead for empty extents was not significant enough to offset the added branch check.

asi.hypothesis: Skip SurrealKV extent range scan when inode.size==0 (new files) — saves a transaction creation + range iterator for first write to each new file
asi.rollback_reason: Slightly worse perf (+2.2%). Range scan overhead for empty extents is small; branch check adds overhead for non-zero-size files. May be noise but discarding since no improvement.

description: Use point reads for single-block extent scans instead of range iterator. No meaningful change (0.3%, within noise).

asi.hypothesis: Use point reads (meta.get_value) instead of SurrealKV range scan when write touches only 1 block. Avoids iterator creation + seek.
asi.rollback_reason: No measurable improvement. SurrealKV range iterator overhead is small for single-block scans.
asi.next_action_hint: Try optimizing hash computation or write batching

description: Use Arc<Vec<u8>> for pending_chunks to share data between chunk_data_cache and compression. Saves one full copy per new chunk but within noise (0.3%).

asi.hypothesis: Share Arc<Vec<u8>> between chunk_data_cache and pending_chunks to avoid one full-copy per chunk. Changed PendingChunk.data from Vec<u8> to Arc<Vec<u8>>.
asi.rollback_reason: Within noise (0.3%). The saving (~4GB of memory operations across 4344 chunks) is only ~0.9s in a 92s benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Look for structural instead of micro optimizations

description: Change stage_chunk_if_missing to take Vec<u8> by value instead of &[u8] to avoid an extra copy. Saves one 1MB alloc+copy per new chunk but regression is within noise (1.5%).

asi.hypothesis: Take Vec<u8> by ownership instead of &[u8] to avoid copy in stage_chunk_if_missing. Saves one full copy per new chunk duration (1MB per block).
asi.rollback_reason: Slightly worse (1.5%), within noise. The saving of 1 copy per chunk doesn't move the needle on this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Try structural change in SurrealKV or pack format

description: [FINAL SUMMARY] Won: -29% from full-block fast path. 6 experiments: 1 kept (-29%), 5 discarded (all within noise). sm_write_dura remains at ~45s — dominated by FUSE overhead + dd process creation + fsync amplification, not VerFSNext data path.

asi.hypothesis: End-to-end performance optimization of VerFSNext read/write
asi.winning_change: Full-block fast path in prepare_write_plan - hash write slice directly instead of zero-fill+copy for new blocks
asi.next_action_hint: Consider pack-header skip on read (saves pread per chunk), or SurrealKV tuning

description: Merge header+payload into single pread in read_chunk_payload_with_index. Saves one syscall per chunk read. Within noise (0.4%). lg_read_rev regressed by 19% — run-to-run variance.

asi.hypothesis: Merge header+payload into single pread in read_chunk_payload_with_index — reduces syscalls per chunk read from 2→1.
asi.rollback_reason: Within noise (0.4%). The syscall saving (~300ns per read for 3000 reads = ~1ms) is too small to measure against run-to-run variance (~3%).
asi.next_action_hint: Try a more impactful structural optimization

description: Add [profile.release] with lto="fat" and codegen-units=1. No measurable improvement (0.4%). Rust already defaults to ThinLTO. Benchmark is I/O-bound, not CPU-bound.

asi.hypothesis: Fat LTO + codegen-units=1 enables aggressive cross-crate inlining, potentially improving hot paths.
asi.rollback_reason: No improvement (0.4%, within noise). Rust release mode already uses ThinLTO. Build time increased from ~10s to ~2m without benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Look for bottlenecks outside the Rust code — the benchmark is I/O and process-creation bound

description: Fix O(n²) memory copies in merge_write_op: add fast path for sequential writes (incoming_start == existing_end) that uses extend_from_slice instead of allocating a new merged buffer each time. For 512 merged 1MB writes, this went from ~131GB of copies to ~1GB. lg_write_dura -24% (19,771→14,958ms).

asi.hypothesis: Add sequential-append fast path to merge_write_op — O(n²) copies from repeatedly allocating merged buffers for coalesced writes was destroying large file write performance.

description: Fix batch config: rename batch_max_blocks→batch_max_size_mb=1024. The old name was silently ignored, causing default 512MB batch size. Larger batches reduce dispatches for large file writes (768MB checkpoint now fits in single batch). lg_write_dura -3.2%.

asi.hypothesis: Fix benchmark config: batch_max_blocks was renamed to batch_max_size_mb but test wasn't updated. The intended larger batch reduces number of dispatches for large files.

description: [CONFIRMATION RUN] Stable at ~88,864ms. 0.6% variance from previous best — confirms the gains are real.

asi.hypothesis: Confirmation run to verify stability of cumulative optimizations

description: [STABILITY RUN] 90,336ms (within 2% of best 88,364ms — normal variance). Diagnostic confirmed: ALL 5890 writes use FUSE_WRITE_CACHE async path (kernel 6.12 properly negotiates writeback cache). Writes don't block — only fsync blocks.

asi.key_finding: FUSE writeback cache IS active (async=5890, sync=0). The earlier estimate of~13s FUSE round-trip overhead was wrong — async writes don't block. Remaining sm_write_dura bottleneck is process creation + fsync + VerFSNext processing.

description: [FINAL SESSION] Stable at ~89,963ms (within 2% of best 88,364). 13 experiments total, 3 kept. Extensive diagnostic confirmed: ALL writes async (FUSE_WRITE_CACHE), all ops <5ms. Remaining ~45s sm_write_dura bottleneck is benchmark shell overhead (3000 dd processes, 3300 printf subprocesses, bash loop), not VerFSNext internals.

asi.key_finding: FUSE writeback cache active (async write path). Remaining bottleneck is benchmark external overhead.

description: Inline compression for small batches (≤4 chunks) to avoid spawn_blocking + rayon overhead. No improvement — the overhead was negligible compared to actual compression work.

asi.hypothesis: Avoid spawn_blocking+rayon overhead for small compression batches (1-4 chunks) by compressing inline.
asi.rollback_reason: Within noise (0.2%). The compress time per chunk (~100µs) dominates the spawn_blocking overhead (~5µs).
asi.next_action_hint: Session has reached diminishing returns on this benchmark
